description: Use it when the user wants to see a video's crop for each place before it renders. Plans what reframe_video renders, without rendering: finds the shots of a finished video and, for each place's shape, a window that follows what moves in each shot, or a padded shot where a crop would cut too much. Writes crop.json, every shot with its window for each shape, sheet.png, each shape's window drawn on every shot's frames (a solid outline for a crop, a dashed one for a padded shot), with more shots in sheet-2.png and on, and FORMATS.md, which the result shows with the command that renders the plan. Look at the sheet, move a window that misses in crop.json, then give that crop.json to reframe_video as crop. A plan in a folder of an earlier render keeps its files. For the files themselves in one job, use reframe_video instead. The reframe playbook (makersmcp_playbook) has the whole job. (reframekit 0.1.4, on this machine.)

brand.description: A brand kit, its folder, brand.json or _brand.yml, for padded shots on its page background color. make_brand_kit makes one.

cover.description: The moment each place's cover shows, in seconds like "4.5" (default: picked).

crop.description: An edited crop.json whose shapes to keep: the plan adds the windows of a place whose shape it has none of. It takes no cuts or steps, and no mode but fit.

cuts.description: Every shot change, in place of those found: seconds like 3.2,7.5, or a JSON file of seconds, of frames with their fps, a launch film's film.timeline.json or a demo's steps.json.

for.description: The places to plan for, in one run at most 12: any of tiktok, reels, shorts, youtube, x, linkedin, feed, square, all (the default) or a size like 1080x1350, as reframe_video takes them.

fps.description: The files' frame rate (default: the video's own), for the render command the plan gives.

lufs.description: The loudness the files will have in LUFS (default -14), for the render command the plan gives.

mode.description: follow crops each shot where what moves is, and pads a shot a crop would cut (default follow); center crops from the middle; pad shows every shot whole; fit keeps the picture's own shape.

out_dir.description: Folder to save into, absolute or relative to /tmp/churn-hnvpfmca. Default: <video-folder>/reframekit-<video-name>, where <video-name> is the name of video without its extension and <video-folder> is the folder video is in. A run replaces the files an earlier run of this kit left there, so give each version its own out_dir. The folder must be empty or hold an earlier run of this kit for the same video: any other folder stops it.

pad.description: What a padded shot sits on: blur (default), black, white, a color like #0f172a, or brand, which needs brand. The render command the plan gives carries it.

seconds.description: Keep at most this long in each place's video, cut at a shot change: seconds like "30", or "1:30". The render command the plan gives carries it.

steps.description: The steps.json of the demo this video is, when it is not beside the video under its name.

trim.description: Set to false never to cut a file to its place's length. The render command the plan gives carries it.

video.description: The finished video, any file ffmpeg reads, like film.mp4 from a launch film or demo.mp4 from a demo. The film.timeline.json or steps.json beside it, under its name, gives its shots.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result, counted from the start of the call, before returning a job_id to wait on. Some clients end a call after 60 or 240 seconds; 45 is safe in all of them.

name: plan_reframe

continued.description: True when this call continued the job an identical call started, instead of starting another.

docs.description: The notes the text shows, and where each one is.

expires_at.description: When the download links stop working.

url.description: Where to download the file, when the job ran on a server.

folder.description: Where the kit saved its files.

last_line.description: What the kit was doing last.

next.description: What to do next, as the Next line says.

passed.description: For checks: whether the check passed.

title: Plan each place's crop
